paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the Servant carried what belonged to us. "We all like sheep have gone astray, each one has turned to his own way; and the LORD has laid upon Him the iniquity of us all" (Isaiah 53:6). The people speaking first thought He was "stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted" (Isaiah 53:4). But they came to see that "He was pierced for our transgressions, He was crushed for our iniquities" (Isaiah 53:5).

Why does that matter to you? Because you don't have to carry your wrongs by yourself, and believe me, I've tried. I once dropped a whole tray of cookies and told myself I could fix it with a spatula and confidence. The passage says "the punishment that brought us peace was upon Him, and by His stripes we are healed" (Isaiah 53:5), and it says He had done no violence and there was no deceit in His mouth (Isaiah 53:9).

And the Servant's story doesn't end in the dark. "After the anguish of His soul, He will see the light of life and be satisfied" (Isaiah 53:11), and He will be "raised and lifted up and highly exalted" (Isaiah 52:13). When Philip met a man reading this very passage, he began with it and told him the good news about Jesus (Acts 8:32-35). So take your hands off the recipe card, friend, and trust the One who bore the sin of many.
